gloss: first three days of the New Year

definitions.gloss: first three days of the New Year (January 1-3)
definitions.explanation: The first three days of January, considered the core of the New Year holiday period in Japan. Most businesses are closed, and families gather for traditional celebrations.

examples.japanese: {三|さん}が{日|にち}は{実家|じっか}で{過|す}ごす。
examples.english: I spend the first three days of the year at my parents' house.

examples.japanese: {三|さん}が{日|にち}の{間|あいだ}はお{店|みせ}が{閉|し}まっている。
examples.english: Shops are closed during the first three days of the year.

examples.japanese: {三|さん}が{日|にち}を{過|す}ぎると、{街|まち}は{少|すこ}しずつ{普段|ふだん}の{様子|ようす}に{戻|もど}っていく。
examples.english: After the first three days, the town gradually returns to its usual routine.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
{三|さん}が{日|にち} (January 1-3) is the most important holiday period in Japan. During this time, families visit shrines ({初詣|はつもうで}), eat traditional New Year dishes ({御節料理|おせちりょうり}), and exchange greetings. Most businesses and government offices are closed.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {正月|しょうがつ}{三|さん}が{日|にち}: the first three days of the New Year
- {三|さん}が{日|にち}の{間|あいだ}: during the first three days

WRITING:
The が in {三|さん}が{日|にち} is usually written in hiragana. The word derives from {三箇日|さんがにち} where {箇|か} is a counter.
